newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast ANS slips, price formula uncertain.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast ANS slips, price formula uncertain.

text.p: U.S. West Coast Alaskan crude prices slipped with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) spot values Thursday, as most traders stayed sidelined until a clear price formula emerged for March deliveries.
BP America, a key producer of the grade, offered Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude at $1.25 below March NYMEX and said bidders were as wide as $1.50 a barrel under.

Players were unable to agree on which basis to use for ANS deals, with NYMEX February crude rolling into the cheaper March contract earlier this week, and thin spot February barrels seen as an unreliable benchmark by regional buyers.
Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude dropped 55 cents to $22.22/22.42 a barrel.
Line 63 crude was bought at $1.00 a barrel over Buena Vista crude postings on Wednesday, the grade's buyer said.
No deals were reported on a fixed basis, but one trader claimed the discount stood about $2.30 to $2.40 below WTI.
Meanwhile, the market for California heavy crudes was talked lower than early week levels, with players hearing trades at 25 to 50 cents below the postings.
